question: Refer to the exhibit. A Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switch has port security configured, and the MAC address table shows three secure MAC addresses learned on Eth1/1 in VLAN 10. An engineer must prevent any newly learned MAC addresses from forwarding traffic on this port, without affecting the MAC addresses that are already secured. Which configuration accomplishes this goal?
explanation: Official answer is B (protect), though community vote leans toward A.
theory: The switchport port-security violation protect action silently drops ingress traffic from any new, nonsecure MAC address once the interface's secure-MAC maximum is reached, without generating a syslog message/SNMP trap or disabling the port - which keeps the three already-secured MAC addresses and their traffic completely unaffected. This differs from 'shutdown' (which err-disables the entire port, blocking all traffic including the already-secured MACs) and from 'restrict' (which drops the traffic but also logs a violation). (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 18 - Nexus Port Security Violations and Actions)
